plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: Dense, cone-shaped clusters of tiny four-petaled flowers weigh down the branches. They give off a sweet, powdery perfume that drifts across gardens, parks and old farmsteads. Each cluster holds hundreds of individual blossoms, and together they make a haze of color against heart-shaped green leaves.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April through May, with peak bloom around mid-May in the northeastern United States. Late-blooming cultivars continue to the end of May.
plants.location: Northeastern United States, including New York, where lilac collections and festivals mark the peak around Mother's Day
plants.funFact: Lilac is a member of the olive family. Breeders have developed hundreds of cultivars, and gardeners can stretch the show over several weeks by planting early, mid and late bloomers.
